theme: Severe mental illness in clinical records
significance: Electronic health record study of 13,391 patients and 35,409 prescribing observations, showing that antipsychotic polypharmacy was associated with endocrine and metabolic adverse drug reactions recorded in routine care.
contribution: Joint first author; I led the analysis and writing.

significance: Ten years of national US treatment provider data showing how geography, organisation, and payment shaped the provision of buprenorphine and methadone. The forerunner of my current work on England's national treatment data.
contribution: First author; I designed and led the analysis.

significance: Audit of how highly cited alcohol research collects and reports data on sexual orientation and gender identity. Our team has since applied the same approach to cardiovascular research (Circulation: Population Health and Outcomes, 2026).
contribution: Senior author; I designed the audit approach and led the methodology.

significance: Repeated national survey data from 579,017 US adults identifying the groups with the greatest unmet need for mental health treatment, and the barriers they reported.
contribution: First author; I led the analysis and interpretation.

significance: National school registry study of more than 7 million pupils in England, showing marked social, ethnic, and geographical variation in recorded autism incidence. Cited in the OECD's 2026 report on rising childhood autism diagnoses, and the basis for my ADR UK fellowship.
contribution: Joint first author; I led the population and spatial analyses.
